SECTION 1. AUTHORITY AND APPLICABLE REQUIREMENTS

1.1 This Subaward is made under the authority of the Community Services and Family Stabilization Block Grant, Assistance Listing Number 93.799, and is governed by 2 CFR Part 200, Subparts A through F, as adopted by the Department.

1.2 The Subrecipient shall comply with 2 CFR 200.303 (Internal controls), 2 CFR 200.302 (Financial management), 2 CFR 200.318 through 200.327 (Procurement standards), and Subpart E (Cost Principles) in the administration of this Subaward.

1.3 In accordance with 2 CFR 200.332, the Department has determined that the Subrecipient presents a moderate risk of noncompliance and will conduct one (1) on-site monitoring visit during the Period of Performance.

SECTION 2. SCOPE OF WORK AND PERFORMANCE TARGETS

2.1 The Subrecipient shall operate a family stabilization program providing housing navigation, benefits enrollment, and emergency financial assistance to households in Northgate and Elwood counties.

2.2 The Subrecipient shall serve not fewer than 240 unduplicated households during the Period of Performance, of which at least 60 percent shall have household incomes at or below 125 percent of the Federal Poverty Guidelines.

2.3 The Subrecipient shall achieve a housing retention rate of not less than 85 percent measured at six months after case closure, as reported in the Department's Family Outcomes Data System.

2.4 Eligibility documentation for every household counted toward the target in Section 2.2 shall be maintained in the client file and shall include verification of income, household composition, and county of residence.

SECTION 3. REPORTING REQUIREMENTS

3.1 Quarterly Programmatic Report. The Subrecipient shall submit a quarterly programmatic report to the Department no later than thirty (30) calendar days after the end of each Federal fiscal quarter. The quarterly programmatic report shall report progress against each performance target in Section 2, the number of unduplicated households served, demographic data in the categories prescribed by the Department, and a narrative describing barriers to performance and corrective steps taken.

Commonwealth of Franklin DHS — Subaward FRA-DHS-2026-CSBG-114 — Page 3 of 6

3.2 Quarterly Financial Report. The Subrecipient shall submit a quarterly financial report on Standard Form 425 (SF-425), Federal Financial Report, no later than thirty (30) calendar days after the end of each Federal fiscal quarter. Each SF-425 shall report cumulative cash receipts and cash disbursements, Federal share of expenditures, unliquidated obligations, and indirect expenses computed at the rate stated on page 1.

3.3 Reporting Schedule. The following due dates apply:

     Quarter 1 (October 1 – December 31, 2026)     reports due January 30, 2027
     Quarter 2 (January 1 – March 31, 2027)        reports due April 30, 2027
     Quarter 3 (April 1 – June 30, 2027)           reports due July 30, 2027
     Quarter 4 (July 1 – September 30, 2027)       reports due October 30, 2027

Both the quarterly programmatic report and the quarterly financial report are due on the dates listed above.

3.4 Final Federal Financial Report. A final SF-425 covering the entire Period of Performance shall be submitted no later than ninety (90) calendar days after the end of the Period of Performance, that is, by December 29, 2027. The final SF-425 must report zero unliquidated obligations.

3.5 Final Performance Report. A final performance report shall be submitted no later than ninety (90) calendar days after the end of the Period of Performance, that is, by December 29, 2027. The final performance report shall summarize cumulative results against every target in Section 2 and shall include the disposition of any equipment acquired under this Subaward.

3.6 Late Reports. The Department may withhold payment on any request for reimbursement submitted while a required report is overdue.

SECTION 4. PAYMENT AND FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT

4.1 Payments will be made on a cost-reimbursement basis. Requests for reimbursement shall be submitted monthly through the Franklin Grants Portal and shall be supported by a general ledger detail report for the period claimed.

4.2 Advance payments are not authorized under this Subaward.

4.3 The Subrecipient shall liquidate all obligations incurred under this Subaward not later than ninety (90) calendar days after the end of the Period of Performance in accordance with 2 CFR 200.344.

SECTION 5. BUDGET AND PRIOR APPROVAL

5.1 The approved budget is set forth in Attachment A. Consistent with 2 CFR 200.308, the Subrecipient shall obtain the written prior approval of the Department before transferring funds among direct cost categories when the cumulative amount of such transfers exceeds ten percent (10%) of the total approved budget.

5.2 The Subrecipient shall obtain written prior approval before changing the scope or objective of the program, before disengagement of the Project Director for more than three months, and before incurring costs more than ninety (90) calendar days before the beginning of the Period of Performance.

5.3 Requests for a no-cost extension must be submitted in writing not less than forty-five (45) calendar days before September 30, 2027.

SECTION 6. AUDIT REQUIREMENTS

6.1 Single Audit. If the Subrecipient expends $1,000,000 or more in Federal awards during its fiscal year, it shall have a single audit or program-specific audit conducted in accordance with 2 CFR 200.501. The reporting package and data collection form shall be submitted to the Federal Audit Clearinghouse within the earlier of thirty (30) calendar days after receipt of the auditor's report or nine (9) months after the end of the audit period.

6.2 The Subrecipient shall provide the Department with a copy of the single audit reporting package, including the schedule of findings and questioned costs, within thirty (30) calendar days of its submission to the Federal Audit Clearinghouse.

6.3 If the Subrecipient does not meet the threshold in Section 6.1, it shall submit a certification of non-applicability signed by its chief financial officer within nine (9) months after the end of its fiscal year.

SECTION 7. RECORDS AND ACCESS

7.1 In accordance with 2 CFR 200.334, the Subrecipient shall retain all financial records, supporting documents, statistical records, and all other records pertinent to this Subaward for a period of three (3) years from the date of submission of the final Federal Financial Report.

7.2 The Department, the Franklin State Auditor, the DFCS Office of Inspector General, and the Comptroller General of the United States shall have the right of access to any pertinent books, documents, papers, and records of the Subrecipient.

SECTION 8. PROCUREMENT AND SUBAWARDS

8.1 All procurement transactions shall be conducted in a manner providing full and open competition consistent with 2 CFR 200.319. The Subrecipient shall maintain written procurement procedures and documentation of the rationale for the method of procurement, selection of contract type, contractor selection or rejection, and the basis for the contract price.

8.2 The Subrecipient shall not issue any subaward under this Subaward without the written prior approval of the Department.

8.3 The Subrecipient shall verify that no contractor or subrecipient is suspended or debarred by checking the System for Award Management exclusions before entering into any covered transaction exceeding $25,000.

SECTION 9. PROGRAM INCOME, EQUIPMENT, AND CLOSEOUT

9.1 Program income earned under this Subaward shall be used under the addition method described at 2 CFR 200.307(e)(2) and shall be reported on each SF-425.

9.2 Equipment with a per-unit acquisition cost of $5,000 or more may not be purchased without written prior approval. Title to equipment vests in the Subrecipient subject to the conditions at 2 CFR 200.313.

9.3 Closeout will proceed under 2 CFR 200.344. The Department will issue a closeout letter after acceptance of all final reports and refund of any unobligated balance.

SECTION 10. GENERAL PROVISIONS

10.1 Nondiscrimination. The Subrecipient shall comply with Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, and the Age Discrimination Act of 1975.

10.2 Termination. This Subaward may be terminated in whole or in part in accordance with 2 CFR 200.340.

10.3 Order of Precedence. In the event of conflict, the following order controls: (a) Federal statute and regulation; (b) this Agreement; (c) Attachment A, Approved Budget; (d) the Subrecipient's application.
